2.content:
This Statement of Work covers Alcon’s ALCON SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 to SAP S/4HANA 2025 On-Premise Upgrade, a fixed-price technical conversion running from June 2026 through March 2028. The engagement includes conversion of the existing ECC environment to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise, migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6, mandatory simplification and remediation activities under a no-change principle, testing and validation across planned conversion cycles, cutover support, change communications, training support, and one month of hypercare for Alcon’s global landscape.

- Execute the ECC to S/4HANA technical conversion and platform migration within the agreed no-change scope.
- Deliver the required remediation, testing, mock conversions, load verification, and cutover activities to support a February 2028 go-live.
- Provide project governance, stakeholder communication, and hypercare support to enable a stable transition into post-go-live support.

<IMAGE id="89f740d3e998"/>

Deferred scope decisions, delivery assumptions, and any draft-specific open items are set out in Section 10 (Key Assumptions) and Section 21 (Key Observations).

3.1.content:
Alcon is undertaking a fixed-price technical conversion of its SAP ECC 6.0 EHP6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise, with a concurrent platform migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6. The program spans 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants, requiring a controlled conversion approach across a large and business-critical footprint.

The engagement is driven by the need to modernize the core ERP platform while preserving business continuity through a no-change principle. The primary delivery challenges are mandatory simplification remediation, custom code and analytics remediation, integration readiness, multiple conversion rehearsals, and production downtime control to a maximum target of 48 hours. The project also addresses earlier gaps in estimation and delivery readiness by tightening integration inventory clarity, defining dependency ownership, and structuring governance, documentation, and multi-vendor coordination for execution through go-live and hypercare.

3.2.content:
- Convert Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 EHP6 environment to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise using a no-change principle.
- Migrate the database and platform from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6.
- Remediate mandatory SAP simplification items, custom code, security impacts, and analytics components required for the target release.
- Execute 10 planned conversion cycles, including mock conversions, load verifications, and dress rehearsal, to de-risk production cutover.
- Validate technical readiness through testing of backup, disaster recovery, high availability, and cutover procedures.
- Achieve production conversion and go-live in February 2028 within the agreed downtime target.
- Provide governance, change communications, training support, and one month of hypercare through transition to Alcon’s steady-state support model.

3.3.content:
The target-state delivery model is a structured brownfield technical conversion executed in phased environments from sandbox through development, quality, mock cycles, technical load verification, dress rehearsal, and production cutover. The converted S/4HANA landscape will retain existing business processes except where mandatory simplification, technical compatibility, security, or platform changes require remediation. Governance, documentation, testing, and readiness controls will be applied throughout to support predictable execution across global operations.

<IMAGE id="c8d8e19bae62"/>

At a high level, the to-be process flow is: month-zero pre-planning and readiness alignment; sandbox screening and remediation planning; system builds and refreshes for DEV and QAS; iterative remediation of simplification items, custom code, security, and analytics objects; repeated mock conversions and load verification cycles to reduce cutover risk; dress rehearsal to confirm production readiness; production conversion and go-live in February 2028; and one month of hypercare before transition to the ongoing support organization.

4.1.content: The services cover Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise technical conversion across North America, EMEA, and APAC. The in-scope landscape supports 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants. Delivery will be performed through a blended model of on-site support in the USA and offshore delivery, including activities required for the Fort Worth data center environment and the global production landscape impacted by the conversion.

4.2.content:
Process scope is limited to remediation and validation required to preserve current-state business process continuity under the no-change principle during the technical conversion to SAP S/4HANA. In-scope process areas are:
- Finance
- Equipment Finance Agreements
- Technical Services
- Materials Management (MM)
- STRM / Warehouse Management
- Sales and Distribution / OTI
- Production Planning (PP)
- Master Data Governance (MDG)

Only mandatory SAP simplification impacts affecting these areas are included. No elective process redesign, process harmonization, or business-led functional enhancement is included.

4.3.content:
Technical scope includes conversion of the existing SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6 environment to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise and migration of the database and platform from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6. In-scope technical activities include sandbox and development screening, SUM/DMO Downtime Optimized Conversion with CustOnTemp, remediation of mandatory simplification items, custom code and development object remediation, security framework updates, add-on and bolt-on alignment, technical testing for backup, disaster recovery, and high availability, and execution of 10 planned conversion cycles including standard and mock runs. Formal quality cycles, technical load verification, dress rehearsal, production cutover, and hypercare support through March 2028 are included.

<IMAGE id="42e72067b696"/>

4.4.content:
Included services are:
- Program and project management for the fixed-price technical conversion
- Detailed planning for month-zero mobilization, environment readiness, and milestone tracking
- Solution design and technical architecture support for the conversion approach
- BASIS, security, ABAP, and analytics remediation delivery
- Conversion execution across sandbox, development, quality, mock, dress rehearsal, and production cycles
- Technical and formal quality testing support, including IQ, OQ, PQ, DILT, and user acceptance coordination
- Cutover planning and production conversion support
- Governance, status reporting, and shared-accountability RACI support
- Change communications, change impact validation, training support, and user adoption tracking
- One month of post-go-live hypercare
- Knowledge transfer to Alcon and handoff to the Bristlecone AMS team by end of hypercare

4.5.content: Application scope covers the existing SAP application landscape components required for the no-change technical conversion and mandatory remediation. In-scope application areas include SAP ECC 6.0 Ehp6, SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise target environment, BASIS, Security, ABAP, and analytics components comprising BW, Datasphere, SAC, and BODS. Functional application coverage is limited to the modules and business areas identified in this SOW where mandatory simplification, remediation, testing, and conversion support are required to achieve go-live readiness. Application functionality not expressly identified as in scope is excluded unless added through approved change control.

5.content:
The proposed architecture is a no-change technical conversion of Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 EHP6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise, including migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to SAP HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6. The solution retains existing business process intent and limits scope to mandatory simplification, custom code remediation, analytics remediation, platform migration, testing, cutover, and hypercare.

The deployment model is based on a phased non-production-to-production conversion path across sandbox, development, quality, mock conversion, load verification, dress rehearsal, and production environments. Execution includes SUM/DMO downtime-optimized conversion, multiple mock cycles, technical load verification, and controlled production conversion against a maximum production downtime target of 48 hours.

<IMAGE id="bd5f7d275ef9"/>

Architecture governance will follow a centralized joint delivery model with integrated oversight across Alcon, Bristlecone, and other relevant partners. Technical, functional, security, basis, analytics, and regional teams will operate through defined ownership boundaries, direct technical-to-technical dependency management, and track-level accountability to support delivery across 53 countries, 90 legal entities, and 18 manufacturing plants.

Change governance will enforce the no-change principle throughout the engagement. Any requested elective change, scope expansion, or deviation from mandatory simplification remediation will be handled through formal change control, with impact assessment on timeline, effort, validation, and downtime before approval. For regulated-scope activities, delivery will align to Alcon’s validation and lifecycle control model, including documented qualification, release readiness, and controlled transition into hypercare and AMS handoff.

6.1.content:
The engagement will be executed as a fixed-price technical conversion using a no-change principle, converting Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 EHP6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise while migrating the database and platform from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6. Delivery will follow a gated lifecycle covering pre-planning, environment preparation, remediation, iterative conversion rehearsals, technical validation, production cutover, and one month of hypercare.

The methodology includes:
- Month zero pre-planning starting at project kickoff in June 2026
- Sandbox, development, and quality environment readiness in sequence
- Mandatory simplification, custom code, analytics, security, add-on, and bolt-on remediation within the no-change scope
- SUM/DMO Downtime Optimized Conversion with CustOnTemp for conversion execution
- Ten planned conversion cycles, including two standard cycles and eight mock cycles
- Technical testing covering backup, disaster recovery, and high availability
- Dress rehearsal before production conversion and go-live in February 2028
- Hypercare through March 2028, followed by transition to the Alcon/Bristlecone AMS support model

Quality assurance will be embedded through phase-based Q-Gates, a pre-deployment readiness check, weekly status reporting, RAID governance, and lessons learned carry-forward between phases.

7.1.content:
Project governance will operate through a centralized joint model across Alcon, Bristlecone, and relevant partner teams, with clear ownership for delivery management, scope and change control, financial tracking, risk management, quality management, and stakeholder communication. The governance structure will include daily stand-ups for delivery execution, daily internal team meetings for issue alignment, weekly PMO meetings for milestone and dependency review, monthly steering committee meetings for executive oversight, and ad hoc meetings for urgent decisions or cross-track resolution.

Level 1 escalation will be managed by the Project Manager and core solution team for day-to-day delivery issues. Level 2 escalation will be managed by the Program Manager for cross-track, schedule, resource, quality, and dependency matters. Level 3 escalation will be raised to executive sponsors, client partner, delivery partner, and Alcon leadership for decisions affecting scope, timeline, budget, business continuity, or go-live readiness. Risks, issues, actions, and decisions will be tracked through the project management controls agreed for the engagement.

- Project leadership and specialist roles shall maintain qualifications and certifications appropriate to their responsibilities, which may include SAP product certifications, Agile or Scrum credentials, change management certifications, and relevant professional qualifications as applicable to the assigned role.

10.content:
- The engagement is a fixed-price technical conversion of Alcon’s SAP ECC 6.0 EHP6 landscape to SAP S/4HANA 2025 on-premise, including migration from Oracle 19c on AIX to HANA 2.0 on Red Hat Linux 9.6, and does not include elective functional change.
- Delivery is based on a no-change principle; only mandatory SAP simplification items and remediation required for technical conversion, compatibility, security, and analytics continuity are included.
- The project timeline assumes June 2026 kickoff, month-zero pre-planning at mobilization, February 2028 production conversion and go-live, and one month of hypercare through March 2028.
- Planning, rehearsals, and cutover readiness are based on 10 conversion cycles, including 8 mock cycles, technical load verification activities, and dress rehearsal before production conversion.
- Production conversion planning, cutover sequencing, and validation are based on a maximum production downtime target of 48 hours.
- Custom code and development object remediation estimates are based on the object counts assumed as of March 2026; any material variance from that baseline will be handled through the Change Management Process in Section 17.
- Alcon will lead source system preparation, system build and refresh coordination, and required Fort Worth data center activities, with Bristlecone providing planned conversion support within the agreed delivery model.
- SAP-side remediation, validation, and cutover support for in-scope interfaces are included; changes to third-party applications, middleware logic, file generation, transmission, scheduling, monitoring, or error handling remain outside scope.
- Validation, testing, and release readiness activities will align to Alcon’s lifecycle and control requirements, including applicable IQ, OQ, PQ, traceability, backup, disaster recovery, business continuity, access management, and security procedures.
- Change communications, training support, and user-readiness activities will align to Alcon’s CCM methodology, and the frequency and intensity of those deliverables depend on the start timing of the assigned Bristlecone OCM resource.
- Hypercare covers one month of post-go-live stabilization only, after which support transitions to Alcon and the Bristlecone AMS team.

| 1 | Deferred scope decisions or late clarification of in-scope remediation, interface ownership, or validation responsibilities delay planned milestones. | Medium | High | Freeze open scope decisions during month zero, maintain a RAID log, assign owners through the agreed governance model, and route any impact to scope, timeline, or commercials through formal change control. |

16.1.content:
Milestone control will be managed through the approved Key Deliverables in Section 9 and the fixed-price commercial structure in Section 13. Each phase gate will be tied to completion of the relevant deliverables, documented acceptance against the defined criteria, and review through the agreed governance forums before progression to the next major milestone.

The milestone baseline is: project charter, project plan, communication plan, RAID log, and governance structure at kickoff in June 2026; sandbox readiness and simplification analysis by September 2026; DEV readiness, configuration and installation documentation, integration adjustment run book, and training plan by November 2026; QAS readiness, test plan and test scripts, and updated testing entry and exit criteria by February 2027; mock conversion and validation deliverables across April 2027, June 2027, and July 2027; technical load verification outputs in August 2027 and October 2027; dress rehearsal report in November 2027; production conversion, go-live, cutover playbook, and hypercare plan in February 2028; and hypercare closure with AMS handover in March 2028.

Commercial tracking shall follow the same milestone structure so that billing, progress reporting, and acceptance remain aligned to completed deliverables rather than informal phase status alone.

16.2.content:

- OCM deliverable cadence and intensity shall be finalized at mobilization based on the confirmed start date of the Bristlecone OCM resource.
- Any decision that would introduce elective changes, non-mandatory simplification, or third-party system logic changes shall be treated as out of scope unless approved through change control.
- Open decisions affecting downtime approach, cutover sequencing, validation effort, or environment readiness shall be closed before the applicable mock, load verification, or dress rehearsal milestone.

16.3.content:
- The no-change principle is the baseline control for integration and custom code scope.
- SAP-side integration work is limited to remediation, validation, and cutover support required for S/4HANA readiness; third-party logic changes remain excluded.
- The in-scope interface inventory shall be frozen during planning and used as the reference baseline for effort, schedule, and acceptance. <CONFIRM: final named in-scope interface inventory>

16.4.content:
All scope, schedule, commercial, and assumption deviations shall be managed through the Change Management Process defined in Section 17. No elective change, additional remediation scope, interface expansion, custom code growth, delivery-model change, or milestone-date revision will be treated as included work unless reviewed for impact and approved through that process.

Change control shall apply to requested changes arising from business decisions, technical findings, dependency shifts, validation outcomes, or governance actions. Each approved change shall document the reason for change, delivery impact, commercial impact, acceptance impact, and any effect on the February 2028 go-live target or the maximum 48-hour production downtime objective.

Where a requested item falls within an exclusion or conflicts with the no-change principle, it shall not proceed without formal written approval under Section 17 and corresponding update to the affected scope, deliverable, and commercial baselines.

This applies in particular to any elective change, any increase in custom code or interface remediation beyond the agreed no-change baseline, any change affecting the ≤48-hour production downtime target, and any deviation from assumptions governing the fixed-price technical conversion.

The request shall describe the change, reason, impacted milestone or deliverable, and required decision date. | Alcon or Bristlecone Project Manager / Program Manager | Within 2 business days of identifying the change |

24.content:
Resource profiles for this engagement shall align to the roles defined in Section 7 and the personnel requirements set out in Section 8. Assigned resources shall be selected for demonstrated experience in large-scale SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA brownfield conversions, platform migration to SAP HANA, mock conversion and cutover execution, regulated validation delivery, and global stakeholder coordination across North America, EMEA, and APAC.

Project and program leadership resources should combine enterprise SAP delivery experience with formal project governance credentials such as PMP, Certified ScrumMaster, or equivalent program and Agile certifications. Functional, technical, and analytics resources should bring relevant SAP delivery experience in the in-scope domains and technologies, including BASIS, Security, ABAP, BW, Datasphere, SAC, and BODS, with role-appropriate SAP product certifications where applicable.

Resources assigned to validation, testing, and quality activities shall have experience with IQ, OQ, PQ, traceability, defect governance, audit-ready documentation, and controlled release readiness in regulated environments.
